items.scope: Prove firstF concavity and monotonicity on [2,4] from explicit derivatives; derive Q convexity, monotonicity and nonnegativity on [0,b-2], and remove the old pointwise hconc premise.
mathematical_review: For firstF(s)=log(s-1)/s, the stated first and second derivatives are algebraically correct. The second numerator is 2(s-1)^2 log(s-1)-2s(s-1)-s^2 and its denominator s^3(s-1)^2 is positive.
On2<=s<=4, log(s-1)<=s-2<=2. Hence the second numerator is <=s^2-6s+4=(s-2)(s-4)-4<=-4, giving the required nonpositive curvature and concavity including endpoints.
For x>=1, G(x)=(x-1/x)/2-log(x) has G(1)=0 and derivative (x-1)^2/(2x^2)>=0. Substituting x=s-1 in[1,3] yields the correct nonnegative first derivative, including s=4.

Q(b,u)=firstF(b)-firstF(b-u) is convex and increasing on the exact u interval[0,b-2] when2<=b<=4. The affine reversal and endpoint u=0 give Q>=0. The pointwise corollary retains positive-coordinate and actual residual-ratio guards from the held parent theorem.
